core1b.fresh_task: A monochromatic beam enters a transparent material from air. The measured wavelength changes from 720 nm to 480 nm. A technician records the incoming angle as 30° to the normal and the outgoing angle as 19.47°, but does not say whether the latter is to the normal or surface. Determine which interpretation is consistent, then predict the speed ratio and explain whether a second normally incident beam alone can verify the index.
core1b.protected_work: Combine independent wavelength and angular observations to identify a consistent optical-index model and reject an ambiguous angle convention.

stages.predict: Before solving, predict the outcome or relationship and record uncertainty.
stages.attempt: A monochromatic beam enters a transparent material from air. The measured wavelength changes from 720 nm to 480 nm. A technician records the incoming angle as 30° to the normal and the outgoing angle as 19.47°, but does not say whether the latter is to the normal or surface. Determine which interpretation is consistent, then predict the speed ratio and explain whether a second normally incident beam alone can verify the index.
stages.reconstruct: Frequency unchanged gives n₂/n₁=720/480=1.5 and v₂/v₁=2/3. Snell gives sin r=sin30/1.5=1/3, r≈19.47° to the normal. If measured to surface, normal angle would be 70.53°, inconsistent. Normal beam remains collinear regardless of index ratio; directional measurement alone cannot verify n.
stages.diagnose: Only if your saved response exhibits this error: Inferring index from bending alone while ignoring wavelength ratio or impossible transmission domain. Otherwise record insufficient evidence.
stages.repair: Use frequency conservation to get index ratio, then test Snell sine domain and angular reference independently.
stages.boundary_test: What optical observation besides direction could verify index at normal incidence?

core1b.fresh_task: A beam travels from unknown liquid into air. Its wavelength rises from 400 to 600 nm. The incident angle is 45° to the normal; a colleague reports an emergent angle of 60°. Use both independent observations to test whether a propagating refracted ray is possible and explain the discrepancy.
core1b.protected_work: Combine independent wavelength and angular observations to identify a consistent optical-index model and reject an ambiguous angle convention.
